issues.legal_issue: A residential tenancy inherited by heirs who normally lived with the deceased tenant does not cease for all of them merely because one heir builds or acquires a separate residence.
material_facts: The deceased tenant’s widow and children had normally lived with him in the residential premises and continued living there after his death.
The heirs who met the statutory definition continued as tenants in their own right, and rent was paid for the premises.
One of the heirs built a separate house and moved into it.
The authorities treated that acquisition as causing the entire tenanted premises to become vacant.
issues.conclusion: The separate house acquired by one heir did not cause the tenancy of the other heirs, who were tenants in their own right, to cease or make the premises vacant. The appeal was allowed, and the contrary decisions were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3(a) and 3(g) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, heirs who normally resided with a deceased tenant in a residential building become tenants in their own right, and “family” is determined by the statutory definition. Under section 12(3), “the tenant or any member of his family” refers to that tenant and members of that tenant’s statutorily defined family; it does not make the heirs a single body of joint tenants whose interests all end when one heir acquires another residence. Personal law and the concept of joint tenancy do not govern this statutory interpretation. The Full Bench decision in Smt. Rama Devi Shakya v. Additional District Judge was overruled.

rule.if: residential_tenancy_vacancy_dispute and heirs_lived_with_deceased_tenant and heirs_qualified_as_tenants_in_own_right and one_heir_acquired_separate_residence

predicates.residential_tenancy_vacancy_dispute: The dispute concerns whether a residential tenancy is deemed vacant because a tenant or a member of the tenant’s family acquired another residence.
predicates.heirs_lived_with_deceased_tenant: The heirs normally lived with the tenant in the residential premises when the tenant died.
predicates.heirs_qualified_as_tenants_in_own_right: The heirs met the statutory conditions to become tenants of the residential premises in their own right.
predicates.one_heir_acquired_separate_residence: One of the heirs built or acquired another residence and moved into it.
predicates.other_qualified_heirs_tenancy_does_not_c: The tenancy of the other heirs who qualified as tenants in their own right does not cease merely because one heir acquired a separate residence.

issues.definition: When a residential-tenancy vacancy dispute involves heirs who lived with the deceased tenant and qualified as tenants in their own right, one heir’s acquisition of a separate residence does not end the other qualified heirs’ tenancy.
